Title: Image Compressor
Description: Compress a JPEG, PNG or WebP image in your browser: set quality 1–100, keep or change the format, compare sizes and download. No upload.

Seo_Introduction: Shrink a JPEG, PNG or WebP image right in the browser: choose a quality from 1 to 100 and an output format, compare the original and compressed sizes, then download the _min file. The image is never uploaded.
Seo_DetailedDescription:
The compressor re-encodes one image at a time. **Keep Original Format** keeps JPEG as JPEG and PNG as PNG and saves any other input as WebP; you can also force JPEG, PNG or WebP. Quality works per format: JPEG uses it directly, PNG below 90 is reduced to a 256-colour palette (90 and above stays lossless), and WebP is encoded lossy by the browser at the chosen quality.

Re-encoding drops EXIF and other metadata such as camera model and GPS location; the EXIF orientation is applied to the pixels first, so phone photos keep their rotation. Transparent areas turn white when you save to JPEG. If the browser has no lossy WebP encoder (some Safari versions), a lossless WebP is saved and a note says the quality setting was not applied.

Compression runs in a Web Worker with Rust/WebAssembly and the browser's own WebP encoder, so the page stays responsive on large images and **Cancel** stops the job immediately. The file is read locally and never sent to a server.
Seo_Examples:
**Photo to WebP**: a 1920×1280 JPEG of `476.38 KB` with **WebP** at quality `80` becomes `186.58 KB` (`Done! -61%`) and downloads as `photo_min.webp`.

**Stronger JPEG**: the same photo as **JPEG** at quality `60` gives `167.27 KB` (−65%); at the default `80` it gives `396.49 KB` (−17%).

**Screenshot**: a 1280×800 interface screenshot (`126.47 KB` PNG) becomes `53.49 KB` as **WebP** at quality `80`, while lossless PNG at quality `90` gives `91.26 KB`.

**Nothing to gain**: if the result is not smaller (for example, an already optimized file), both sizes are shown but the `Done!` badge stays hidden — keep the original.
Seo_HowToSteps:
### Step 1: Choose an image
Click **Choose file** or drop a PNG, JPEG or WebP image onto the zone. A thumbnail with the file size and dimensions appears.

### Step 2: Set quality and format
Move the **Quality** slider (default 80%) and pick an **Output Format**: **Keep Original Format**, JPEG, PNG or WebP.

### Step 3: Compress
Click **Compress Image**. A long job can be stopped with **Cancel**.

### Step 4: Compare and download
Check **Original:** → **Compressed:** and click **Download** to save `<name>_min.<ext>`.
Seo_Tips:
- For photos, WebP or JPEG at quality 60–80 usually saves the most; keep PNG for screenshots and graphics with transparency.
- PNG below quality 90 switches to a 256-colour palette: fine for flat graphics, but gradients may band and the file is not always smaller.
- Saving a transparent PNG as JPEG fills the transparent areas with white; choose PNG or WebP to keep transparency.
- EXIF data, including GPS coordinates, is removed from the result — useful before publishing photos.
- If you see the note about lossless WebP, your browser cannot encode lossy WebP; pick JPEG for a smaller photo.
ErrorUnsupportedFormat: This image format is not supported. Use PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, ICO, TIFF or TGA.
WebpLosslessNote: Your browser can't encode lossy WebP, so a lossless WebP was saved and the quality setting was not applied. Choose JPEG for a smaller photo.
